items.stem: A $1,400 hotel bill would need director approval. A colleague suggests two claims of $700. What do you do?

options.text: Split it so your manager can approve it
options.feedback: Splitting one expense to stay under a limit is never allowed.

options.text: Submit it as one claim with the real amount
options.feedback: Right: one expense, one claim, real amount.

options.text: Leave out the receipt to keep it simple
options.feedback: Expenses over $25 always need the itemised receipt.

items.explanation: Never split one expense into several claims to stay under an approval limit (§6).
items.scenario: You stayed four nights at a hotel for a client project; the bill is one expense of $1,400.

items.stem: Your approver asked a question about your claim. By when must you answer?

options.feedback: Correct: otherwise the claim is returned to you.
30 days is the submission deadline, not the reply deadline.
After 5 business days the claim is returned to you.

items.stem: A hotel night of $250 is fine without any extra approval.

options.feedback: Hotels are capped at $220 per night.
Correct: above $220 needs a written Travel Desk exception.

items.explanation: Hotel costs are capped at $220 per night unless the Travel Desk approves an exception in writing.
